pull_requests.title: Fix numerical, model-state, and persistence conformance failures

assessment.title: Fix numerical, model-state, and persistence conformance failures
assessment.change: Repair nine causes across supplied regression model state, cosine scaling, PCA total-variance denominator, decoder registered weight paths and batched rotary execution, ANOVA centering, compensated OLS stationarity refinement and valid multi-feature Core ML scaler pipelines.
assessment.default_or_opt_in: Repairs affect existing routes automatically. CPU OLS always computes compensated residual gradient after dgels and can attempt three refinements. Cosine search alone uses scaled arithmetic; other metrics retain their paths. Multi-feature export alone expands to scalar stages. No accuracy-selection option is introduced.
assessment.total_cpu_time_evidence: No matched CPU-time or repair-only throughput series found. Passing CPU regression policy here means no new conformance failure identities; it is not a CPU-resource benchmark. Combined later precision/compact numbers cannot be attributed to this repair PR.
assessment.memory_evidence: OLS adds columnScales, compensated gradient state and candidate/correction vectors, all proportional to feature count rather than rows. Cosine allocates scaledQuery. PCA retains one scalar totalVariance. Supplied regression initializers create public Float MLX parameter arrays. Core ML pipeline serialization grows with feature count and may add rename stages. ANOVA removes flattened all-values and per-group centered arrays.
assessment.new_work_retention_parallelism: OLS adds a column-max scan, initial full residual/gradient scan and up to three candidate residual/gradient scans plus triangular corrections. Cosine adds max-absolute scans and divisions to avoid norm under/overflow. Randomized PCA adds centered sum-of-squares traversal; exact SVD paths sum already available singular/eigenvalues. Scaler exports create one stage per feature and extra identity stages for overlapping names. No new thread scheduling.
assessment.reduced_work_copies: ANOVA uses lazy residual sequences and compensated scalar reductions instead of flattening groups and allocating centered copies. Other costs principally restore correctness.
assessment.correctness_constraints: Preserve existing references/tolerances. Tiny/large nonzero vectors must keep valid cosine, truncated PCA ratios must use all fitted variance, registered checkpoint weights must load, model-state constructors must predict, OLS stationarity must improve on difficult fixtures and serialized Core ML must load with overlapping names. Earlier failing answers are invalid alternatives.
assessment.disposition: Retain repairs. OLS extra scans are a concrete cost worth qualifying on ordinary workloads, but evidence does not establish a regression per correct result.
assessment.next_useful_test: Measure CPU fit time and allocation bytes on ordinary and difficult OLS datasets over rows/features; preserve oracle stationarity and coefficient checks. Any skip criterion must prove unchanged numerical acceptance. Separately qualify scale-safe cosine with overflow/underflow fixtures.

pull_requests.title: Add Apple silicon reduction policies and decimal-preserving ANOVA

assessment.title: Add Apple silicon reduction policies and decimal-preserving ANOVA
assessment.change: Add centered SIMD moments without an input-sized temporary; reuse them in ANOVA; use BLAS ddot for performance-policy vectors >=4096 when count fits Int32; add opt-in compensated dot with exact fallback and decimal-string ANOVA ingestion.
assessment.default_or_opt_in: Existing two-argument dot remains performance mode, Double throughout. Compensated dot and decimalGroups are explicit caller choices. Existing Double variance and ANOVA use CenteredMoments automatically, with old finite-range fallback behavior.
assessment.total_cpu_time_evidence: No operation-scoped total CPU series. Raw precision-kernels memory-before-time.txt and memory-after-time.txt each report only 0.01 user + 0.00 sys seconds at coarse precision for a separate one-shot process. Retired instructions are 320108116 before and 331971079 after, about 3.7% more for the whole process, not an isolated kernel count. These receipts include process startup/input work and cannot resolve kernel CPU cost. Kernel wall-time experiments show variance 4.242 to 4.421 ms at 8388608 values and 0.515 to 0.550 ms at 1048576; small cases are also slower. Default dot and medium/large ANOVA wall times improve in recorded experiments.
assessment.memory_evidence: Default finite centered variance removes one 8-byte-per-element array. At 8388608 elements, RSS falls 140722176 to 73580544 bytes in separate one-shot receipts, about 64 MiB. RSS is a process peak, not ownership. Exact dot uses two 67-limb UInt64 magnitudes, 1072 logical bytes excluding metadata; no input-sized product array. Decimal ingestion materializes residual Double groups and temporary digit/string values.
assessment.new_work_retention_parallelism: Default centered moments add compensated arithmetic and may do partial work before fallback. Performance ddot may have implementation-specific native threading; environment limits do not prove actual threads. Opt-in compensated mode checks products/cancellation and can restart the full reduction exactly. Decimal mode parses bounded strings and performs exact common-origin subtraction before binary64 conversion.
assessment.reduced_work_copies: Removes centered variance buffer and uses bounded SIMD accumulators. ANOVA reuses the blocked routine instead of compensated scalar within-group loops. Performance dot uses existing Accelerate kernels and reads arrays directly.
assessment.correctness_constraints: Actual binary64 variance example changes 67.578125 to correct 67.5703125. Compensated mode has a stronger useful accuracy goal but no universal correct-rounding guarantee; overflow/underflow/cancellation fallback is required. Decimal differences lost before a Double call cannot be recovered. Original decimal and binary64 workloads retain distinct references and tolerances.
assessment.disposition: Measured default variance latency cost buys correctness and about 64 MiB less temporary storage. Expensive compensated dot and decimal ingestion are opt-in and cannot be called default regressions. Faster wrong/cancelled or pre-rounded results are not equivalent comparators.
assessment.next_useful_test: Repeated paired CPU-time, latency and owned-allocation measurements of default variance on ordinary and offset inputs, with exact binary64 oracle. Sweep BLAS crossover sizes and actual thread use. Compare compensated/decimal alternatives only at the same numerical contract.

assessment.change: Direct target extraction, shared feature-type resolution, owned compact Double batches with optional validity bitmaps and row maps, matrix layout export, snapshot-safe updates, concrete scaler integration and scratch reuse.
assessment.default_or_opt_in: New PreparedNumericBatch APIs are opt-in, but existing target extraction, concrete DataFrame standardScale/minMaxScale conveniences and concrete scaler DataFrame overloads change automatically. Existing row-array APIs reuse scratch. Generic PreprocessingTransformer adapter keeps row-array dispatch and now converts once for fitTransform.
assessment.total_cpu_time_evidence: No measured total CPU series found. Historical 100000-row standard-profile medians compare separate desktop sessions: target 3.958542 to 0.058083 ms, standard scaling+flat export 28.393000 to 2.785333 ms, minmax 33.164708 to 0.751166 ms. Matching workload/input contracts support descriptive latency improvement, not a controlled CPU-efficiency or universal baseline. Raw standard responses contain elapsed_ns and RSS.
assessment.memory_evidence: Compact payload is 8 bytes per row per column plus optional ceil(rows/64)*8 validity bytes. Retaining a batch alongside its source adds owned compact buffers. Single-column matrix export shares the values via array copy-on-write; wider matrices pack into new contiguous arrays. ColumnValues and DataFrame replacement materialize optionals. Snapshot mutation detaches shared edited buffers. PayloadByteCount excludes row maps, capacity and metadata and is not total retained memory.
assessment.new_work_retention_parallelism: Preparation converts selected optional columns into owned Double buffers. Row selection gathers new columns and maps original row indices. Multi-column matrix export packs again. Scalers allocate transformed dense columns; MinMax keeps shifted/scaled row-length scratch, Standard uses bounded row-width scratch with gathers/scatters. DataFrame output reconstructs optional columns. No new parallel scheduling.
assessment.reduced_work_copies: Target extraction avoids N one-element rows. Concrete scaler DataFrame fitTransform prepares once, avoids nested rows and reuses workspaces. Row-array scaler scratch moves outside row/column loops. Consumers retaining prepared batches can reuse columns across operations; immediate optional round trips can still pay conversions.
assessment.correctness_constraints: Int64-to-Double precision stays unchanged; valid NaN differs from missing while prepared. Scaling treats missing as NaN and outputs valid numeric NaNs rather than preserving validity. StandardScaler retains row-width vDSP operations for finite rounding compatibility. Preserve repeated features/selections, row identity, matrix order, atomic rejection and array snapshot semantics.

assessment.next_useful_test: Versioned setup-inclusive first-use and reused prepared workflows with CPU time, copied/allocation bytes and retained source+batch+matrix ownership. Include sparse edits with/without snapshots, layouts, missingness and immediate DataFrame materialization.

assessment.memory_evidence: Raw 32768-token checkpoint diagnostics show peak MLX allocation 14769330192 to 5093079072 bytes, 13.76 to 4.74 GiB. One fallback result is budgeted because Core ML output backing is advisory. Extra prepared reservation is 0.189 MiB at 1024 rows and 1.033 MiB at 8192 rows.
memory.limitations: Public CoreMLPredictor loads before per-request admission, so its model state is separately caller-accounted. withPool admits before loading. Queued inputs and escaped output lifetimes remain caller-accounted. Max sampled RSS 144.5 MiB does not establish physical savings, peak allocation or leak freedom. Core ML may make internal copies.

assessment.correctness: Exclusive slots, owned output and immutable retained input prevent concurrent mutation/alias reuse. Shape/name/type/finite checks and drain-before-release remain required. Float16 requires macOS15, has separate accuracy limitations, and CPU/Neural-Engine permission does not prove placement. Direct/prepared parity is within a policy/artifact, not Double-reference equivalence.
assessment.disposition: Retain as an explicit reuse option. One-use overhead and retained storage are documented costs; no automatic preparation threshold or existing-path regression is introduced.
assessment.next_test: At the same model/precision/compute policy and correctness target, report full-lifetime CPU seconds, conversion/memcpy allocations and retained owned bytes across reuse counts; measure device work separately and include model load/release as distinct phases.

pull_requests.title: Bound Core ML inference from loading through consumption

assessment.title: Bound Core ML inference from loading through consumption
assessment.change: Reserve a complete pull-source workflow before model/source loading, bound all loaded-but-unconsumed batches and hold quota through ordered awaited consumption. Subdivide admitted capacity using private preparation budgets.
assessment.default_scope: New explicitly configured CoreMLBatchPipeline.run only. Window and native-slot widths have no automatic policy. Existing reusable prepared inputs remain unchanged.

cpu_time.details: Sustained benchmark provides steady rows/s, not CPU seconds; includes read/decode/preprocess/inference/hash/consume, excludes model load and first 32 completions. 8192-row CPU serial/window2-slot1/window4-slot2 medians are 2.52/5.14/5.36 million rows/s. Greater overlap is not proof of less total work. Source replays one held-out cycle with cache reuse.

memory.benefit: A single count includes queued inputs, running tasks and out-of-order completed outputs until consumption. Private budgets avoid reacquiring a fully held parent quota. Pipeline-only input owners free storage/reservations deterministically after prediction.
memory.new_work_or_retention: Holds whole-run quota for source duration; allows up to configured window batches, tasks and completed-output dictionary entries. Larger windows increase potential live inputs/results. Row-index metadata also costs work: source capacity checks materialize originalRowIndices for identity inputs; prepared ownership separately copies row mapping.
memory.observations: 32-case peak sampled RSS 163.75 MiB, largest second-half range 1.72 MiB; 4096-batch confirmations peak 152.64 MiB CPU and 130.92 MiB CPU+Neural-Engine policy. Traces show allocation steps followed by plateaus. File adapter autorelease correction reduced 128-read growth 436 MiB to 0.59 MiB, but belongs to benchmark tooling, not production pipeline.
memory.limitations: These are bounded-run observations, not leak proof or allocator-enforced RSS caps. Caller retained results/source/consumer workspace still require estimates. More concurrent loaded batches deliberately retain more storage.

assessment.correctness: Awaited ordered consumption preserves sequence and original row identity. Fixed model batches must match exactly; no padding/truncation/retries. Structured child/native drain before quota release remains necessary on error/cancellation; callback-boundary cancellation does not prove device interruption.
assessment.disposition: Keep as a bounded overlap option. Its benefit is a count/lifetime bound and throughput choice, not established minimum total CPU or device energy.
assessment.next_test: Measure total CPU seconds and owned live bytes for windows1/2/4 at the same slot count, with slow/out-of-order consumption and long input streams; separate device work and investigate row-index metadata allocations without weakening row provenance.

pull_requests.title: Retain Core ML models across separately admitted batch runs

assessment.title: Retain Core ML models across separately admitted batch runs
assessment.change: Retain a model/pool across sequential bounded runs while separately reacquiring the batch-window work partition, sharing the previous rolling scheduler.
assessment.default_scope: New explicit withSession/session.run option. Caller chooses chunk size and distinct lifetime/work budgets; prior whole-run API remains. No automatic model scheduler or default change.

cpu_time.details: Final 144 measured samples report total elapsed, service/admission/completion time and RSS, not summed CPU seconds. Tight 8192-row neural-policy whole-run/retained 8 medians 1326.58/1387.43ms, while maximum observed peer wait 466.53/23.36ms. Thus eight-batch retained runs trade 4.6% more elapsed for 95% less maximum observed peer wait. They avoid reload 8 total 1707.25ms. Not a CPU/energy reduction claim.

memory.benefit: Keeps one model/pool setup rather than recreating every short run, while releasing work quota between caller-bounded runs so CPU/GPU peers can enter.
memory.new_work_or_retention: Lifetime reservation covers model/pool buffers and context through session scope, even while idle. Final fixture partitions 49 MiB lifetime plus 64/128/192 MiB work; unused lifetime allowance cannot be lent to work. Each run still reserves its entire window.
memory.observations: Peak sampled RSS 179.61 MiB across final comparison; every partition drained/reacquired, including 12 active/queued cancellation checks.
memory.limitations: Fixed-partition fairness/latency choice, not a universal optimum, starvation guarantee, physical-memory cap or leak certificate. Fixtures are outside reservations but inside RSS. Persistent startup precedes peers; total/first completion include it, admission waits exclude it. Neural policy permits CPU fallback.

assessment.correctness: Reject overlapping session runs before admission, enforce distinct budgets and sufficient work capacity, preserve failed-run reuse, then drain callbacks and native predictions before releasing lifetime. Sequence numbers restart per run; callers keep cross-run identity if needed.
assessment.disposition: Keep as an explicit responsiveness option. Longer-lived model retention is intentional, bounded and separately charged; no demonstrated introduced default resource regression.
assessment.next_test: At equal total allowance and correct per-policy results, compare full-session CPU seconds and retained owned bytes against reload and whole-run options; report startup, idle residency, run chunk size, peer latency and device activity separately.
